summary: Half of the Georgia knowledge exam is the Road Signs test, and it is given in English only. This chapter covers the basics: what each sign shape and color means, and how to read the signs that state rules you must obey.

Shape comes first. The eight-sided sign is used only for STOP, and the triangle pointing down is used only for YIELD. Upright rectangles are usually rule signs, such as SPEED LIMIT, while wide rectangles are usually guide signs that show directions and places. Diamonds warn, the five-sided sign marks a school zone or crossing, and the round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead.

Color tells you the job of the sign. Red is used for STOP, YIELD, DO NOT ENTER, and WRONG WAY. Green signs guide you, blue signs show services such as gas and lodging, brown signs lead to parks and recreation, and orange signs mark construction and maintenance work. A red circle with a slash over a picture means the action shown is not allowed.

Some rule signs come with Georgia turning rules. You may turn right on a steady red light after a complete stop unless a sign forbids it, and you may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street going left. Where NO TURN ON RED is posted, wait for green. On multi-lane roads, slower traffic must keep right and leave the passing lane.

concepts.definition: A red eight-sided sign. Stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can best see oncoming traffic. Then yield and go when it is safe.
concepts.tip: Eight sides: stop all the way, every time.

concepts.definition: A red and white triangle pointing down. Slow down, stop if needed, and let vehicles in the intersection or close to it go first.
concepts.tip: Triangle pointing down: give way.

concepts.definition: Signs that state rules you must obey just like traffic laws, such as SPEED LIMIT, ONE WAY, DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and NO TRUCKS. Most are upright white rectangles. A red circle with a slash means the action shown is not allowed.
concepts.tip: White rectangle: a rule, not a suggestion.

source.org: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (FHWA)

concepts.definition: Red: stop, yield, and do not enter. Yellow: general warning. Orange: construction and maintenance. Green: directions and guide signs. Blue: services. Brown: parks and recreation.
concepts.tip: Orange means workers; blue means services.

source.org: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (FHWA)

concepts.definition: Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on a steady red light after a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians. A left turn on red is allowed only from the left lane of a one-way street onto a one-way street whose traffic moves to your left.
concepts.tip: Right on red after a full stop; left on red only one-way to one-way.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Traffic Laws)

concepts.definition: On a road with two or more lanes in your direction, slower drivers must move out of the left (passing) lane when faster traffic comes up behind them, even if they are at the speed limit.
concepts.tip: Left lane is for passing, not cruising.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Slow Poke law)

points: The eight-sided sign is used only for STOP.
The triangle pointing down is used only for YIELD.
Upright rectangles state rules; wide rectangles guide you.
A red circle with a slash means the action shown is not allowed.
Where NO TURN ON RED is posted, wait for the green light.
Blue signs show services; orange signs mark work zones.

compare.title: Turning on a steady red light
rows: Stop completely and yield to traffic and pedestrians
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left
Stop completely, yield, and stop for pedestrians
Any turn where NO TURN ON RED is posted

summary: Warning signs tell you about a hazard or a change in the road before you reach it, so you have time to slow down. This chapter covers yellow diamond warning signs, school signs, railroad crossing signs, the no passing pennant, and orange work zone signs.

Most warning signs are yellow diamonds with black words or symbols, and some are fluorescent yellow-green. A T shape means the road you are on ends and you must turn left or right. A merge sign shows traffic joining your road. A smoothly bending arrow means a curve, and a yellow plaque with a speed under the sign gives the advised safe speed for it.

Some warning signs use other shapes. The five-sided sign marks a school zone or school crossing. The round yellow sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead, and the white X-shaped crossbuck stands at the tracks themselves, sometimes with a plate showing how many tracks there are. The yellow pennant on the left side of the road marks the start of a no passing zone.

Orange signs mark work zones. In a work zone a flagger has the same authority as a regulatory sign, and you must yield to work vehicles with flashing amber lights. Speeding past a regulatory speed limit in a Georgia work zone can bring a fine of $100 to $2,000.

concepts.definition: The usual shape and color for warning signs. It warns of a hazard or a change ahead, such as a curve, a merge, a road that ends, or a slippery road. Some warning signs are fluorescent yellow-green.
concepts.tip: Yellow diamond: something is coming, slow down.

source.org: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (FHWA)

concepts.definition: A yellow plaque with a speed, placed under a warning sign. It shows the advised safe speed for that curve or hazard, which is usually lower than the speed limit.
concepts.tip: Yellow number under a curve sign: slow to that speed.

concepts.definition: The five-sided (pentagon) sign marks a school zone or school crossing. It may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green.
concepts.tip: Five sides, like a schoolhouse.

source.org: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (FHWA)

concepts.definition: The round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. The white crossbuck stands at the crossing, where you must yield to trains. A plate under the crossbuck may show the number of tracks.
concepts.tip: Round sign: tracks ahead. Crossbuck: tracks here.

concepts.definition: A yellow sign shaped like a sideways triangle, placed on the left side of the road. It marks the beginning of a no passing zone, so finish any pass before you reach it.
concepts.tip: Pennant on the left: no passing from here.

concepts.definition: Orange signs mark construction and maintenance work. A flagger has the same authority as a regulatory sign. Yield to work vehicles with flashing amber lights. Speeding past a regulatory work zone speed limit can bring a fine of $100 to $2,000.
concepts.tip: Orange means workers: slow down and obey the flagger.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Highway Work Zones)

concepts.definition: An orange triangle with a red border on the back of a vehicle. In Georgia it marks a vehicle that moves at less than 25 mph, such as farm equipment.
concepts.tip: Orange triangle on a tractor: slow down early.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Signs, Signals and Markings)

points: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards or changes ahead.
A T-shaped symbol means your road ends; get ready to turn left or right.
The five-sided sign means a school zone or school crossing.
The round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.
The pennant on the left side of the road starts a no passing zone.
In a work zone, obey flaggers just as you obey regulatory signs.

compare.title: Railroad crossing signs and markings
rows: Round yellow sign with X and RR
X and RR painted on the road
On the pavement before the crossing
Yield to trains; a plate may show the number of tracks

figures.caption: The round sign and the painted X warn you before the tracks; the crossbuck stands at the tracks.

summary: This chapter covers traffic signals, lane control and pedestrian signals, and the lines painted on the road. Signals and markings appear on the Road Signs test along with signs, so learn what each light and line asks you to do.

A steady red light means stop and wait for green. A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red, so slow down and prepare to stop. A green light lets you go only after you yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection. A flashing red light is treated like a STOP sign, a flashing yellow light means slow down and go with caution, and a flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic. If a signal is completely dark, treat the intersection as a stop in every direction.

Some signals control lanes or people walking. Over reversible lanes, a green arrow means you may use the lane, a steady yellow X means move out of it, a flashing yellow X means it is for left turns, and a red X means do not drive in it. A pedestrian hybrid beacon stays dark until someone presses the button, and its alternating flashing red lights mean stop, then go when the crosswalk is clear.

Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions, and white lines separate lanes going the same way. A broken yellow center line allows passing when safe, a solid yellow line on your side means you may not pass, and double solid white lines mean no lane changes. The center two-way turn lane is only for left turns, and you may enter it no more than 300 feet before your turn.

concepts.definition: A flashing red light means stop completely, then go when it is safe, as at a STOP sign. A flashing yellow light means slow down and go through with caution.
concepts.tip: Flashing red = STOP sign. Flashing yellow = caution.

concepts.definition: If a traffic signal is not working at all, every driver must treat the intersection as if a stop sign were posted in every direction.
concepts.tip: No lights at all: all-way stop.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Traffic Signals and Signs)

concepts.definition: You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Oncoming traffic still has a green light.
concepts.tip: Flashing yellow arrow: turn only in a safe gap.

concepts.definition: Signals over each lane of a reversible lane system. Green arrow: travel in the lane. Steady yellow X: clear the lane. Flashing yellow X: left turn permitted. Red X: no travel in that lane in your direction.
concepts.tip: Red X over a lane: stay out of it.

concepts.definition: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line allows passing when safe. A solid line on your side means you may not pass. Two solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction.
concepts.tip: Solid line on your side: no passing for you.

concepts.definition: A center lane bordered by solid and broken yellow lines, used only for left turns by traffic from both directions. You may enter it no more than 300 feet before your turn.
concepts.tip: Center turn lane: left turns only, within 300 feet.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Pavement Markings)

concepts.definition: White dashed lane lines separate lanes going the same direction, and you may cross them when safe. Double solid white lines mean lane changes are not allowed. A white stop line shows where to stop.
concepts.tip: White = same direction. Yellow = opposite direction.

points: Flashing red: stop, then go when safe. Flashing yellow: slow down and use caution.
A signal that is completely dark means stop in every direction.
A flashing yellow arrow allows a left turn only after yielding.
A red X over a lane means do not drive in that lane.
A solid yellow line on your side of the center means you may not pass.
The center two-way turn lane is only for left turns.

compare.title: Yellow center lines on a two-lane road
rows: Allowed when safe, in either direction
Broken line on your side, solid line on the other side
Solid line on your side, broken line on the other side

figures.alt: Three short two-lane road sections seen from above. The first has a single broken yellow center line, the second has a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, and the third has two solid yellow lines. Each has a label explaining when passing is allowed.
figures.caption: The yellow line closest to your lane tells you whether you may pass.

summary: Right of way is about who should go first, and it is always something to give, not take. This chapter covers intersections, driveways, pedestrians, school buses, emergency vehicles, and Georgia's Move Over law.

At an intersection with no signs or signals, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrived, and if two arrive together, yield to the one on your right. When you turn left, yield to oncoming traffic. When you enter a road from a driveway or private road, stop and yield to everyone already on the road or sidewalk. In a roundabout, yield to traffic already circling.

Pedestrians in a crosswalk must be given the right of way. Stop and stay stopped when a pedestrian is on your half of the road or within one lane of it, and never pass a car that has stopped at a crosswalk. Always yield to a person with a white cane or guide dog.

When a school bus shows flashing yellow lights, get ready to stop. When its red lights flash and the stop arm is out, stop, unless you are on the other side of a highway divided by a median. For an emergency vehicle with lights and siren, pull to the right and stop. For a stopped emergency, sanitation, or utility vehicle with flashing lights, move over a lane or slow down below the speed limit.

concepts.definition: An intersection with no stop signs, yield signs, or signals. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
concepts.tip: Same time, no signs: yield to the right.

concepts.definition: All drivers yield to pedestrians, then go in first-to-arrive, first-to-go order. If two vehicles arrive at about the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.
concepts.tip: First to stop, first to go; tie goes to the right.

concepts.definition: Stop and stay stopped when a pedestrian in a crosswalk is on your half of the road or within one lane of it. Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. On a multi-lane road, stop at least 10 feet before the crosswalk.
concepts.tip: Your half of the road means every lane going your way.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Sharing the Road)

concepts.definition: Flashing yellow: the bus is about to stop. Red lights and stop arm out: you may not pass. On a highway divided by a median, only traffic going the bus's way must stop. Stay stopped until the bus moves or its signals go off and children have cleared.
concepts.tip: Red lights on a bus: stop, unless a median divides you.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Sharing the Road)

concepts.definition: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights and siren, move to the right shoulder or as far right as you can and stop, without blocking an intersection. Do not follow a fire truck answering an alarm closer than 200 feet.
concepts.tip: Lights and siren: pull right and stop.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Traffic Laws)

concepts.definition: For a stopped emergency, tow, sanitation, or utility vehicle with flashing lights, move over to the next lane if you safely can. If you cannot, slow down below the speed limit and be prepared to stop.
concepts.tip: Flashing lights on the shoulder: move over or slow down.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Move Over law)

points: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic.
Leaving a driveway or private road: stop and yield to everyone on the road and sidewalk.
A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog always has the right of way.
In a roundabout, yield to traffic already circling.
Across a median, you need not stop for a school bus on the other side.
Move over a lane, or slow below the limit, for stopped vehicles with flashing lights.

compare.title: When you must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing
rows: No need to stop, but watch for children

summary: This chapter covers Georgia's general speed limits, the Super Speeder law, how to pass safely, and the places where you may not park. Many questions here are about numbers, so learn them as a set.

When no other limit is posted, Georgia's general limits are 30 mph in urban or residential districts, 35 mph on unpaved county roads, 70 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates and multi-lane divided highways, and 55 mph in all other areas. A driver convicted of 75 mph or more on a two-lane road, or 85 mph or more on any road, is a Super Speeder and pays a $200 state fee on top of the local fine.

Pass only where it is legal and safe, and be back in your lane before oncoming traffic comes within 200 feet. Passing on a two-lane road is not allowed within 100 feet of a railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct, or tunnel, on hills or curves where you cannot see, or on the shoulder. When someone passes you, do not speed up.

Georgia law keeps parked cars away from places where they would block safety. Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal, or 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Never park on a sidewalk, in an intersection, or on a bridge.

concepts.definition: Unless posted otherwise: 30 mph in urban or residential districts, 35 mph on unpaved county roads, 70 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates and multi-lane divided highways, and 55 mph in all other areas.
concepts.tip: 30 town, 35 dirt, 55 other, 65 urban interstate, 70 rural interstate.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Speed Limits)

concepts.definition: A driver convicted of speeding at 75 mph or more on a two-lane road, or 85 mph or more on any road. A $200 state fee is added to the local fine. If it is not paid on time, the license is suspended and a $50 reinstatement fee is added.
concepts.tip: 75 on two lanes or 85 anywhere: $200 extra.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Super Speeder)

concepts.definition: Return to your lane before the passing zone ends and before oncoming traffic is within 200 feet. Do not pass within 100 feet of a railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct, or tunnel, on a hill or curve where you cannot see, or on the shoulder.
concepts.tip: 200 feet from oncoming cars, 100 feet from crossings and bridges.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Passing)

concepts.definition: Allowed when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and there is enough room, or on a road with two or more lanes going your way. Never pass on the shoulder.
concepts.tip: Right-side passing needs real pavement, never the shoulder.

concepts.definition: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or signal, 20 feet of a fire station driveway (75 feet across the street), or 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
concepts.tip: Hydrant 15, crosswalk 20, stop sign 30, railroad 50.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Stopping, Standing, and Parking)

concepts.definition: On a sidewalk, within an intersection, on a crosswalk, on railroad tracks, on a bridge or overpass, on a controlled-access road, or where a sign forbids it. A disabled car that cannot be moved off the road should leave a clear view for 200 feet each way.
concepts.tip: Sidewalks, intersections, tracks, and bridges: never.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Stopping, Standing, and Parking)

points: Georgia's general limit in urban or residential districts is 30 mph.
Rural interstate 70 mph; urban interstate or multi-lane divided highway 65 mph.
Super Speeder: 75 mph on a two-lane road or 85 mph on any road.
Finish passing before oncoming traffic is within 200 feet.
When being passed, do not speed up.
Parking: hydrant 15 feet, crosswalk 20 feet, stop sign 30 feet, railroad 50 feet.

compare.title: Parking distances to remember
rows: Stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal
Across the street from a fire station driveway

summary: This chapter collects the safe driving habits and equipment rules that appear on the Road Rules test: headlights, following distance, bad weather, emergencies, expressways, seat belts, the Hands-Free law, and sharing the road with bicycles, motorcycles, and trucks.

Use headlights from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise and whenever it is raining, and dim your high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle. Check your following distance by counting one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two after the car ahead passes a mark. Leave more room at night and in bad weather, and three or four seconds behind a motorcycle.

Wet roads are most slippery in the first half-hour of rain, and partial hydroplaning can begin at about 35 mph. In a skid, ease off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid. In a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and let the car slow. In fog, use low beams. On an expressway, never back up, and stay in the acceleration lane until the solid white line ends.

Everyone in the front seat and every rider under 18 must wear a seat belt, and children under 8 need a proper child restraint. Under the Hands-Free law, you may not hold or support a phone while driving. Give a bicycle at least 3 feet when passing, and remember that if you cannot see a truck driver's face in the mirror, the driver cannot see you.

concepts.definition: Required from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, at any time it is raining, and when visibility is low. Dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
concepts.tip: Rain or dusk: lights on. Oncoming car within 500 feet: low beams.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Use Headlights Properly)

concepts.definition: Count "one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two" after the car ahead passes a fixed point. If you reach the point first, you are too close. Leave more space at night, in bad weather, and in heavy traffic, and three or four seconds behind a motorcycle.
concepts.tip: At least two seconds; more behind motorcycles.

concepts.definition: Leave at least 3 feet between your vehicle and the bicycle. If you cannot change to a lane not next to it, slow to 10 mph below the posted limit or 25 mph, whichever is more.
concepts.tip: 3 feet always; slow down if you can't change lanes.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Passing Bicycles)

concepts.definition: The first half-hour of rain is the most slippery. Partial hydroplaning can begin at about 35 mph. In a skid, ease off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid.
concepts.tip: Rain starts: slow down. Skid: steer where the back slides.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Safety Guidelines)

concepts.definition: Everyone in the front seat must wear a seat belt, and so must every rider under 18 in any seat. A child under 8 must ride in a child restraint that fits the child's height and weight.
concepts.tip: Front seat or under 18: belt. Under 8: child seat.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Safety Belts)

concepts.definition: A driver may not hold or support a phone with any part of the body, or write, send, or read texts, or watch videos while driving. Earpieces and mounted devices are allowed. A first conviction brings 1 point and a fine of up to $50.
concepts.tip: Phone in your hand while driving: illegal.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Hands Free Georgia Law)

concepts.definition: Large blind spots at the sides, front, and rear of trucks and buses. If you cannot see the driver's face in the truck's side mirror, the driver cannot see you.
concepts.tip: Can't see the driver's face? You're hidden.

points: Headlights: half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise, and in rain.
Dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
Pass a bicycle with at least 3 feet of space.
Seat belts: everyone in the front seat and every rider under 18.
Never hold your phone while driving.
Never back up on an expressway; go to the next exit.

summary: Georgia's teen driver law, known as TADRA, created a graduated licensing program in three steps: the Class CP instructional permit, the Class D provisional license, and the full Class C license. This chapter covers what each step requires and the limits on teen drivers.

You can get a Class CP permit at 15 by passing a vision test and the knowledge exam. If you are under 18, you must show proof of school enrollment, and a parent, guardian, or responsible adult must sign. That person can ask to have your permit revoked any time before you turn 18. With a permit, you may drive only with a licensed Class C driver at least 21 years old in the seat beside you.

At 16 you can apply for a Class D license after holding the permit for one year and one day. Joshua's Law requires driver education (30 hours of class plus 6 hours with a certified instructor or the Parent/Teen Driver Guide) and 40 hours of supervised driving, including 6 at night. You also need the Alcohol and Drug Awareness Program (ADAP) and a road test.

A Class D driver may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. Passengers are limited: immediate family only for the first six months, one non-family passenger under 21 for the next six months, and up to three after that. A driver under 21 convicted of offenses such as reckless or aggressive driving loses the license for six months. At 18 you can hold a full Class C license.

concepts.definition: Available at age 15 after a vision test and the knowledge exam. You may drive only with a person at least 21 who holds a Class C license, is fit to take control, and sits in the seat beside you.
concepts.tip: Permit at 15; supervisor 21+ beside you.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Teen Driving Laws)

concepts.definition: Available at 16 after holding the permit for one year and one day, finishing Joshua's Law driver education, 40 hours of supervised driving (6 at night), and ADAP, and passing a road test.
concepts.tip: 16, one year and a day, 40 hours with 6 at night.

source.org: Georgia DDS, Teen Drivers

concepts.definition: Requires a DDS-approved driver education course for a Class D license at 16 or 17: 30 hours of classroom or approved online instruction, plus 6 hours with a certified instructor or the DDS Parent/Teen Driver Guide.
concepts.tip: 30 hours of class plus 6 hours of driving lessons.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Teen Driving Laws)

concepts.definition: A Class D license holder may not drive between 12:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. There are no exceptions.
concepts.tip: Midnight to 5 a.m.: no driving, no excuses.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Teen Driving Laws)

concepts.definition: First six months: immediate family only. Second six months: one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family. After that: up to three passengers under 21 who are not immediate family.
concepts.tip: Family only, then 1, then 3.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Teen Driving Laws)

concepts.definition: A conviction for offenses such as reckless driving, aggressive driving, racing, hit and run, or any 4-point violation suspends the license of a driver under 21 for six months for a first conviction and twelve months for a second.
concepts.tip: Under 21: serious violation means losing the license.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Teen Driving Laws)

points: Class CP permit at 15; Class D at 16; full Class C at 18.
Hold the permit one year and one day before a Class D license.
Joshua's Law: 40 hours of supervised driving, 6 at night.
Class D: no driving from midnight to 5 a.m.
Class D passengers: family only, then one, then up to three non-family under 21.

Passengers under 21 who are not immediate family

summary: This chapter covers Georgia's alcohol limits, the implied consent law, and the point system. These rules decide when a driver loses the license, so the numbers are worth learning exactly.

A driver 21 or older is under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, and a driver under 21 at 0.02 or more. A person driving a commercial motor vehicle faces disqualification at 0.04. Any drug, including a prescription medicine, that makes you unsafe to drive also counts. By driving in Georgia you agree to state chemical tests, and refusing one suspends your license for at least one year.

Points are added for moving violations. Speeding 15 to 18 mph over is 2 points, 19 to 23 over is 3, 24 to 33 over is 4, and 34 or more over is 6. Reckless driving is 4 points, and passing a stopped school bus or aggressive driving is 6. Your license is suspended at 15 points in 24 months, or at 4 points in 12 months if you are under 18. A certified 6-hour driver improvement course can remove up to 7 points once every 5 years.
After any crash, stop in a safe place and help anyone who is hurt. Notify the police right away if anyone is injured or killed, or if property damage is more than $500.

concepts.definition: Under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more for drivers 21 and older, and 0.02 or more for drivers under 21. Driving a commercial motor vehicle at 0.04 or more leads to disqualification.
concepts.tip: 0.08 adults, 0.04 commercial, 0.02 under 21.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Driving Under the Influence)

concepts.definition: Driving in Georgia means you agree to state chemical tests of your blood, breath, urine, or other bodily substances. Refusing suspends your license for at least one year, and the refusal may be used as evidence.
concepts.tip: Refuse the test: lose the license for a year or more.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Implied Consent)

concepts.definition: For a first DUI by a driver under 21, a BAC of 0.02 to less than 0.08 brings a suspension of at least 6 months. A BAC of 0.08 or more, or a refusal, brings at least 12 months. No limited permit is available.
concepts.tip: Under 21: even a little alcohol means a long suspension.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Teen Driving Laws)

concepts.definition: 15 to 18 mph over: 2 points. 19 to 23 over: 3 points. 24 to 33 over: 4 points. 34 or more over: 6 points.
concepts.tip: 2-3-4-6 as the speed climbs.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (The Points System)

concepts.definition: A license is suspended at 15 points in 24 months. A driver under 18 is suspended at 4 points in 12 months, and a driver under 21 for any 4-point violation.
concepts.tip: 15 in 24 months; under 18, just 4 in 12.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (The Points System)

concepts.definition: A licensed Georgia resident who completes a certified 6-hour driver improvement (defensive driving) course may have up to 7 points removed, once every 5 years.
concepts.tip: 6-hour course: up to 7 points off, once in 5 years.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Points Reduction)

concepts.definition: Stop in a safe place, help anyone injured, and notify the nearest law enforcement agency right away if anyone is injured or killed or property damage is more than $500.
concepts.tip: Injury, death, or over $500 damage: call the police.

source.org: Georgia DDS Drivers' Manual (Crashes)

points: BAC limits: 0.08 for 21 and older, 0.02 under 21, 0.04 in a commercial vehicle.
Refusing a state chemical test: at least a one-year suspension.
15 points in 24 months suspends a license; under 18, 4 points in 12 months.
Passing a stopped school bus and aggressive driving are 6 points each.
A prescription is no defense if the medicine makes you unsafe to drive.
